title: Does ten divided by three ever end?
description: Ten is divided by three by long division, and the leftover of one comes back at every place. Keeko doubts that the division ends after two places.
teaching_notes: One idea: when the same leftover comes back, the same digit comes back, and the division never ends. Watch for children who stop after two or three places and call that the answer.

source: Find 10 ÷ 3 by long division. Will it end?
video_script.why: The child has carried long division past the decimal point, but every division so far ended with nothing left over.
video_script.substitution: the book's own long division of ten by three, solved place by place
video_script.anchor: Ten divided by three, by long division
video_script.wrong_move: A common slip stops after two places and writes three point three three. Three times that is only nine point nine nine, which is less than ten.
video_script.payoff_line: Ten divided by three never comes to an end.

final_answer.spoken: three point three three three, and it never ends

maths_rules: 10 Ones ÷ 3 gives 3 Ones, since 3 × 3 = 9, and 10 − 9 = 1 One remains
1 One = 10 Tenths; 10 Tenths ÷ 3 gives 3 Tenths, since 3 × 3 = 9, and 10 − 9 = 1 Tenth remains
1 Tenth = 10 Hundredths; 10 Hundredths ÷ 3 gives 3 Hundredths, since 3 × 3 = 9, and 1 Hundredth remains
the remainder is 1 at every step, so 10 ÷ 3 = 3.333... never ends
the slip: 3 × 3.33 = 9.99, which is less than 10
video_script.design: One idea: the leftover of one comes back at every place, so the division never ends. Assumes long division with a decimal quotient. Wrong idea: stopping after two places. The long division frame stays all video; the working builds place by place; the quotient appears only on the answer beat.
